Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for `judge-branch-audit-e2e-docs`

Clarification mapping
- Clarification set: none.
- Interpreted answer: `/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` means proceed with full scoped implementation.

Conflict notes (issue vs current code)
- `review_autofix.yml` already checks out PR head (`ref: pull_request.head.sha`), so PR-head judge context is already correct there.
- `orchestrate_poll.yml` intentionally checks out default branch (documented exception in `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py`), so integration-branch correctness must be enforced inside `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, not at workflow checkout level.
- README already contains `ORCHESTRATOR_MAX_CLARIFY_CYCLES` and `ai:blocked` mentions; required work is precision/operational wording updates, not first-time additions.

1. Judge-path audit and fixes
Files likely to change
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
- `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py` (or a nearby contract test file)
- `tests/test_review_autofix_merge_precheck.py` (or a new focused workflow contract test)

Functions/modules to implement/update
- In `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, add/extend a helper to prepare judge execution ref per tracking issue before the main wave judge (`mode-judge.txt`) runs.
- Reuse existing integration-context resolution semantics (`resolve_active_orchestrator_context_for_issue`, `integration_branch_exists`, `resolve_branch_analysis_ref`) to select integration branch when metadata exists.
- Enforce fail-safe behavior: if integration metadata exists but branch is missing, do not silently fall back to default branch; keep/extend the existing failure path.
- Keep review-blocked branch-prep behavior as-is unless a real gap is found; add tests to lock it.
- For `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` + `review_autofix.yml`, keep behavior unchanged and add regression coverage proving PR-head context remains required.

Data structures affected
- No schema changes expected.
- Possibly add/adjust runtime log lines for selected judge ref/context per tracking issue to make test assertions deterministic.

API/interface changes
- No external API changes.
- No env-var changes expected.

2. Regression test: integration-only symbols
Files likely to change
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
- Test harness internals in the same file (`_run_poller`, mock git/codex behavior)

Planned test design
- Build a sandbox fixture where a required sentinel symbol/file exists only on `orchestrator/project-<id>` branch, not on `main`.
- Trigger the orchestrator wave judge path.
- Assert judge execution context resolves to integration branch and the sentinel is visible to judge-time execution.
- Assert no default-branch fallback when integration metadata exists and branch is valid.
- Add negative assertion for missing integration branch metadata/branch-missing behavior (fallback only when metadata absent).

3. End-to-end smoke extension
Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`

Planned extension
- Add an orchestrator-managed smoke scenario that includes non-default-branch-only sentinel content in fixture repo flow.
- Assert pipeline advances (plan/progress labels/comments) instead of clarify-loop churn.
- Keep existing smoke flow intact; add as an additive phase/check to avoid destabilizing current release gate.

4. Documentation updates
Files likely to change
- `README.md`

Planned updates
- Tighten `ORCHESTRATOR_MAX_CLARIFY_CYCLES` behavior text with explicit escalation semantics.
- Tighten `ai:blocked` operational semantics for orchestrator clarify-loop guard.
- Add explicit integration-ref resolution order wording:
  - child issue metadata footer first,
  - tracking issue metadata second,
  - default-branch fallback only when integration metadata is absent (not when present-but-invalid).

5. Risks and edge cases
- Poller processes multiple tracking issues per run; branch context must be reset/switched per tracking issue to avoid cross-project bleed.
- Review-blocked merged follow-up behavior intentionally retains default-base fallback when no integration metadata exists; must preserve backward compatibility.
- Branch existence checks can fail transiently; logic must fail open only where already intended and fail closed where metadata mandates integration branch safety.
- E2E additions can be flaky under rate limits; keep assertions on durable phase progression signals.

6. Testing and verification
Targeted tests during implementation
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -q tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -q tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py`
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -q tests/test_review_autofix_merge_precheck.py` (or whichever workflow contract file is updated)

Required full verification for this issue
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -q`
- `bash scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh --self-test`
- `bash -n scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
- `bash -n scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`
